description: Follow-up to catseye-fov. interpreter.ml:matches_sink (line 86-91) does plain substring matching when the pattern does not start with $. This means any short sink pattern (e.g. 'try', 'read', 'exec', 'get', 'set') can match unintended call names that contain the pattern as a substring (e.g. 'RateLimiter.retry_after' matches 'try', 'bread' would match 'read'). The catseye-fov fix patched one instance (SilentErrorSwallow on Crystal) by adding a language filter, but the underlying substring matching is a latent class of bugs likely affecting many other rules. Fix: add an 'exact' modifier (or anchored '^pattern$' syntax) to KDL sinks so rules can opt into exact/prefix matching. Update loader.ml to parse the new field, update interpreter.ml:matches_sink to honor it, audit the existing ruleset to identify which sinks would benefit, and add regression tests. This is a non-trivial engine change that should ship with a CHANGELOG note and a migration guide for rule authors.
title: matches_sink substring matching is a class of false-positive bugs: add exact-anchor support
